city_center.name: Downtown Louisville (West Main cast-iron district) + Old Louisville
city_center.landmark: West Main Street's cast-iron facades (one of the largest such collections in the US) and Old Louisville's Victorian mansions; Churchill Downs to the south
city_center.notes: Ohio River bourbon-and-Derby city. Kroger (Cincinnati-based, dominant across KY) is the home grocer. Old Louisville is the largest preservation district of almost entirely Victorian architecture in the US. sources: louisvilleky.gov West Main cast-iron; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Louisville; gotolouisville.com architecture.

featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: Kentucky apples (Jul-Dec) + Kentucky sorghum; bourbon-barrel-spice tie (flavor only, no alcohol claim)

languages.reason: Spanish is the leading second home language across the Louisville metro. Percentage INFERRED (localization pipeline data absent) -- not an ACS figure

cultural_notes: Louisville is defined by bourbon and the Kentucky Derby (Churchill Downs, first Saturday in May), with the mint julep as its signature drink -- a strong seasonal cultural anchor (source: general regional knowledge; language selection flagged INFERRED)

Downtown Louisville's West Main Street holds one of the largest collections of cast-iron building facades in the US, and Old Louisville is the largest US preservation district of almost entirely Victorian architecture (source: louisvilleky.gov West Main; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Louisville; gotolouisville.com)

Kentucky apples run July through December and sorghum is a traditional mountain-and-farm sweetener; Kentucky's produce peaks with tomatoes and corn in summer and apples and squash in fall (source: kyagr.com Farm Market Produce Availability Guide; farmflavor.com Kentucky produce calendar)
